subject.title: Multi-agent orchestration is unstable: concurrent agents add/config overwrites, session-lock failures, and detached child work

question: Which canonical contract should own the remaining #43367 work before more automated fixes are queued: durable subagent delivery, single-owner fallback/session-lock ownership, or a maintainer-split set of focused issues?
rationale: The remaining behavior changes delivery guarantees, duplicate-prevention, timeout/cancel semantics, lock reclaim safety, and parent/child context contracts, so automation should not choose the permanent product/API boundary alone.

options.title: Split And Sponsor Canonical Contracts
options.body: Keep #43367 open as the umbrella, designate focused canonical owners for durable delivery, fallback ownership, same-PID locks, and metadata-only completion, then land narrow PRs against those contracts.

options.title: Prioritize PR #86540 As A Slice
options.body: Rebase and prove the open lock-stall PR as a near-term durability improvement while explicitly leaving active-run steering, fallback parent-lane ownership, and metadata-only completion to follow-ups.

options.title: Collapse Into One Broad Redesign
options.body: Treat the cluster as a single multi-agent orchestration redesign, accepting slower delivery and higher review cost to settle all cross-surface semantics together.

recommendation.title: Split And Sponsor Canonical Contracts
recommendation.body: Keep #43367 open as the umbrella, designate focused canonical owners for durable delivery, fallback ownership, same-PID locks, and metadata-only completion, then land narrow PRs against those contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest history across subagent delivery, steering, and session-lock policy boundaries among the sampled likely owners.
